content.text:
The Source Control spinner was four abandoned commits, not a broken git install. Command-line git was fine the whole time, and it still is.

Cursor’s commit button runs `git commit --file -` and then waits until that process exits. Each of those four was stuck inside Entire’s `prepare-commit-msg` hook:

- Oct 24, 4:04pm
- Oct 24, 8:36pm
- Oct 24, 8:42pm
- today, 12:06pm

The Cursor process that started them is already gone, but the hook processes kept running. Source Control will not refresh staging or finish a commit while one of its own git processes is still open. A terminal commit uses `git commit -m`, so it never entered that wait, which is why pushes showed up in the repo while the panel kept spinning.

Those four processes are stopped. `git status` in houdini-wizard returns immediately again. The panel itself still has the old spinner in memory, so reload this window once: Command Palette, then **Developer: Reload Window**. After that, stage and commit from the panel again.

To keep the next button-click from hanging the same way, Entire’s `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, and `post-commit` hooks in houdini-wizard, price-wire, squad-builder, and trail-sketch now run with stdin closed. Cursor holds that stream open for the commit message, and the hook was waiting on it. If you later run `entire enable`, it will rewrite those hooks, and this one-line change would need to be put back.

The blurry Start menu icon is a separate result of the Cursor update from October 23. The executable’s own icon is 32×32, which is why the tile looks soft. The app’s real icon file goes up to 256×256. Both Start menu shortcuts now use that file, and the icon cache was refreshed. Open the Start menu again. If a pinned taskbar button is still soft, unpin it and pin Cursor from the Start menu entry so it picks up the sharp icon.

content.text:
Session tracking is still on. Agent sessions and commit checkpoints both still go through Entire.

Live agent sessions are recorded by Cursor’s Entire hooks in `.cursor/hooks.json`. Those were not changed. They still call Entire on session start, each prompt, stop, and session end. This chat’s session was recorded that way after the earlier cleanup.

Commits still run the same Entire git commands, with the same arguments:

- `prepare-commit-msg` still receives the commit message file and adds the checkpoint trailer.
- `commit-msg` still receives that file.
- `post-commit` still condenses the session onto the commit.
- `pre-push` still uploads the session logs. That hook was left unchanged, because git sends the list of refs on stdin.
- `post-rewrite` was also left unchanged, so amend and rebase still keep session links.

The only edit was closing stdin on the first three of those, in houdini-wizard, price-wire, squad-builder, and trail-sketch. Git gives those hooks their data in files, not on stdin. Closing stdin stops them waiting on the pipe Cursor leaves open for the commit message. It does not skip Entire.

Stopping the four hung hook processes removed commits that had never finished. Existing session data and checkpoints were left in place.

content.text:
It came back because Entire was waiting for a yes/no answer that the Source Control panel never shows. Closing stdin did not stop that.

These repos were set up before Entire’s default changed, so commit linking is still in **prompt** mode. On a commit made while an agent session is active, `prepare-commit-msg` asks whether to link that commit to the session. It asks on the Windows console, not on standard input. Cursor is a desktop app, so that console is hidden and nobody can answer. Entire CLI 0.11.4 then waits forever, and the Commit button keeps spinning until that process exits. A terminal commit works because that window can actually receive the answer.

The commit that stuck at 2:44pm was still sitting in that prompt. That process is stopped, and the commit itself was not created.

Linking is now set to **always** in `.entire/settings.local.json` for houdini-wizard, price-wire, trail-sketch, and squad-builder. Those files are local and are not committed. Entire will add the checkpoint trailer on its own and will not ask. The commit hook also tells Entire not to open a terminal prompt. Session recording and commit checkpoints stay on.

Retry the commit from Source Control. If the button is still spinning, run **Developer: Reload Window** once, then commit again.
